chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Hammond and Alexander arrive at the Wichita dance
summary: They slip in unseen and approach at intermission, delighted with the program.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: So anyway I heard from him perhaps one time, but that night we went on to Wichita and set up and all and we were in the back end, the bandstand was in the back of the hall, and so we kicked off right on time and fortunately we had a pretty nice dance. Some of the dances wouldn't be good, but we came in real quick and we played it and nobody saw no John Hammond around or Willard Alexander either. So Melvin asked again, he was more concerned than anybody because he said it wasn't John Hammond. So he says, where's your buddy John Hammond? I said I don't know Mel. Well I told you I thought that was just some cat fooling you. So I said I don't know. We had didn't have an intermission.

We played on and at intermission-- it was during those days, you see Preston, I know that is a little before you were in the business, but after all they had seats all around the wall but they didn't have tables like

everybody had, in the middle there. They really came there to dance and they would sit down for a little while around the wall. So when we had intermission, the people would get to the side and sit down and the floor was open then and we looked there and there walked Alexander and Hammond.

They came on up and so naturally I went to greet them and Hammond introduced (inaudible). So I asked him, how long have you been here? Oh, we've been here while you were playing a couple of numbers. I told the people at the door I was expecting you and they welcomed us in and we just took a seat back there.

Hammond was like a little kid, practically, he just said--he said, Alexander just wanted to just see how you were going to work your program and you sure had a nice program and everything. He was just tickled.
